    #    mode we care most about, and it is the one 120s cannot fix.
    if _DAILY_RE.search(text):

    #    without a 401/403.
    if code in _AUTH_STATUSES:

    if re.search(
        r"invalid[_\s-]?api[_\s-]?key|incorrect[_\s-]?api[_\s-]?key"

        re.IGNORECASE,
    ):

    # 3. Transient rate limit.
    if code == 429 or _TRANSIENT_RE.search(text):
        return TRANSIENT_RATE_LIMIT

    # 4. Server-side / timeout. Explicitly NOT exhaustion.
    if code in _SERVER_STATUSES or _looks_like_timeout(text):
        return SERVER_ERROR

    # 5. Safe default.
    return UNKNOWN

        """A fresh import (proxy restart) must still see the cooldown.

        import importlib
        import litellm_cooldown_persistence as persistence

        persistence.store_cooldown("dep-1", p.DAILY_QUOTA, 3600.0)
        assert state_file.exists()

        reloaded = importlib.reload(persistence)

def capability_tokens(capability: str) -> List[str]:
    """Search tokens for a capability phrase.

    Two bugs lived here. The first version filtered on `len(t) > 2`, which drops
    "ai" — so the escape hatch that was supposed to let AI-assistance match an
    assistant config file could never fire, and the scan silently returned zero
    observations while looking like it had run. The second is that a hard minimum
    length is the wrong rule: a capability is not a bag of long words.

    Tokens are now all words of 2+ characters, minus scaffolding, and the caller
    decides how to combine them. Two characters is kept deliberately: "ai", "js",
    "go" and "r" are load-bearing capability tokens, and dropping them is how
    "AI coding assistance" ends up matching nothing.
    """
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", str(capability or "").lower())
    stop = {"the", "a", "an", "of", "for", "in", "on", "to", "and", "or", "with",
            "how", "many", "much", "do", "you", "have", "has", "had", "years",
            "year", "experience", "experienced", "using", "use", "used", "please",
            "tell", "work", "working", "is", "are", "am", "that", "this", "your",
            "my", "me", "been", "was", "were", "at", "it", "as", "be", "or"}
    seen, out = set(), []
    for tok in text.split():
        if len(tok) < 2 or tok in stop or tok in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(tok)
        out.append(tok)
    return out


def _file_matches(path: Path, tokens: Sequence[str], *, size_cap: int = 200_000) -> bool:
    """True when the filename carries a capability token, or its content does.

    Content search is what makes the scan general rather than a filename
    whitelist. A capability like "ai coding assistance" has no filename that
    contains it; the evidence lives inside AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Matching only
    paths would report "no evidence" for a capability that is plainly present in
    the working tree, which is indistinguishable from a true negative.
    """
    name = path.name.lower().replace("_", " ").replace("-", " ")
    if any(t in name for t in tokens):
        return True
    try:
        if path.stat().st_size > size_cap:
            return False
        body = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").lower()
    except Exception:
        return False
    return any(re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(t) + r"\w*", body) for t in tokens)

                   candidate: str = "rastinder",
                   identity: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
                   max_files_per_repo: int = 4000) -> ActivitySignal:

def _file_matches(path: Path, tokens: Sequence[str], *, size_cap: int = 200_000) -> bool:
    """True when the file evidences the capability, using AND semantics.

    Two mistakes are encoded as explicit rejections here.

    Substring/prefix expansion. An earlier version matched `\\b` + token + `\\w*`,
    so the token "ai" matched "said", "detail", "email", "main", "chain" and
    "aim". That produced 904 "observations" for "ai coding assistance", most of
    them a captcha PNG. A capability is a conjunction of terms, not one fuzzy
    substring, so matching requires EVERY token to appear as a whole word.

    OR semantics. Matching any single token is what let unrelated project files
    in. AND is stricter, which is the correct direction: a false negative falls
    through to journey_estimate or an attested answer where a human or the user
    can correct it, while a false positive is submitted to an employer.
    """
    if not tokens:
        return False
    name = path.name.lower()
    if all(t in name for t in tokens):
        return True
    try:
        if path.stat().st_size > size_cap:
            return False
        body = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").lower()
    except Exception:
        return False
    return all(re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(t) + r"\b", body) for t in tokens)


def _repo_file_dates(repo: Path, emails: set, *,
                     max_entries: int = 60_000) -> Dict[str, Tuple[str, str, int, bool]]:
    """first/last commit date per path, in ONE git invocation per repo.

    The first version shelled out to `git log` once per candidate file. For a
    capability that matched 900 files that was 900 subprocesses and 38 seconds,
    which would have stalled a job application. One `git log --name-only` pass
    builds the whole map, and the cost becomes proportional to history size
    rather than to how loosely the matcher performs.
    """
    out: Dict[str, Tuple[str, str, int, bool]] = {}
    try:
        res = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(repo), "log", f"--max-count={max_entries}",
             "--format=@@%ad|%ae", "--date=short", "--name-only"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    except Exception:
        return out
    cur_date, cur_email = "", ""
    for line in res.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("@@"):
            cur_date, _, cur_email = line[2:].partition("|")
            cur_email = cur_email.strip().lower()
            continue
        p = line.strip()
        if not p or p.startswith("@@"):
            continue
        author_ok = (not emails) or (cur_email in emails)
        prev = out.get(p)
        if prev is None:
            out[p] = (cur_date, cur_date, 1, author_ok)
        else:
            first, last, n, ok = prev
            out[p] = (min(first, cur_date) if cur_date else first,
                      max(last, cur_date) if cur_date else last,
                      n + 1, ok or author_ok)
    return out

fixed:
def enforce_context_floor(entries: list[dict],
                          doc_context: dict | None = None,
                          nv_context: dict | None = None,
                          last_resort_chain: list | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Final gate on the EMITTED model_list.

    Discovery-side filtering is not enough: entries carried over from the
    previous config (and hand-added ones) never pass through discovery, so the
    floor has to be applied again where model_list is written.

    This gate REPAIRS rather than only discards. A Cloudflare entry that
    reaches it without a context_window is a real model whose limit the provider
    docs already published, so `doc_context` is used to backfill it before the
    floor is applied. Previously the gate was purely destructive and lost 7 of
    18 freshly registered models this way (glm-5.3, kimi-k2.7-code,
    gpt-oss-120b, ...) even though their real limits were known. A carried-over
    NVIDIA entry is repaired the same way from `nv_context`.

    An entry whose context cannot be established is still dropped: an unknown
    window is not evidence of a large one.

    The ONE exemption is the local last resort. It is a 98,304 ctx model on a
    10GB GPU, i.e. below MIN_CONTEXT_LENGTH, and it exists for exactly the case
    where every cloud key is dead — so stripping it would leave the chain with
    no floor to fall through to. The exemption is deliberately narrow and has to
    survive review, so it requires all three of:
      1. the explicit `local_last_resort` marker in model_info, AND
      2. a loopback local api_base, so no cloud entry can qualify, AND
      3. LAST-RESORT POSITION in `last_resort_chain` — a trailing, unbroken run
         of marked local entries. A local entry anywhere else in the chain is
         held to the floor like everything else.
    `last_resort_chain` defaults to None, which means NO exemption at all, so
    every other caller of this gate keeps its current strict behaviour.
    """
    exempt = last_resort_position(last_resort_chain, entries)
    kept, dropped, exempted = [], [], []
    for e in entries or []:
        info = e.get("model_info") or {}
        ctx = _num(info.get("context_window"))
        if ctx is None:
            params = e.get("litellm_params") or {}
            model = str(params.get("model") or "")
            if model.startswith(("cloudflare/", "openai/@cf/", "@cf/")):
                truth = _num((doc_context or {}).get(cf_doc_slug(model)))
                if truth is not None:
                    info["context_window"] = int(truth)
                    info["context_source"] = "provider-docs"
                    e["model_info"] = info
                    ctx = int(truth)
            elif "nvidia" in str(params.get("api_base") or ""):
                truth = _num((nv_context or {}).get(model.replace("openai/", "")))
                if truth is not None:
                    info["context_window"] = int(truth)
                    info["context_source"] = "provider-api-limit-error"
                    e["model_info"] = info
                    ctx = int(truth)
        if (e.get("model_name") in exempt) and is_local_last_resort_entry(e):
            # Recorded in the entry, not inferred, so the exemption is greppable.
            info = dict(e.get("model_info") or {})
            info["local_context_floor_exempt"] = True
            info["context_floor_exempt_reason"] = (
                f"last-resort local entry at {int(_num(ctx) or 0)} ctx "
                f"< {MIN_CONTEXT_LENGTH} floor, kept only as the chain's tail")
            e["model_info"] = info
            exempted.append(e)
            kept.append(e)
            continue
        (kept if (ctx is not None and ctx >= MIN_CONTEXT_LENGTH) else dropped).append(e)
    if exempted:
        log(f"  config write: {len(exempted)} local last-resort entries EXEMPT from the "
            f"{MIN_CONTEXT_LENGTH} context floor (kept in the chain's tail): "
            + ", ".join(f"{d.get('model_name')}@{int(_num((d.get('model_info') or {}).get('context_window')) or 0)}"
                        for d in exempted[:8]))
    if dropped:
        log(f"  config write: dropping {len(dropped)} entries below the "
            f"{MIN_CONTEXT_LENGTH} context floor: "
            + ", ".join(str(d.get("model_name")) for d in dropped[:14]))
    return kept

# llama.cpp / llama-server vendor extensions. These are NOT OpenAI SDK
# parameters: AsyncCompletions.create() has a fixed signature, so passing one as
# a top-level kwarg raises
#   TypeError: create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'chat_template_kwargs'
# and kills the whole request. They belong in the JSON request body, which is
# what the SDK's extra_body is merged into.
LLAMA_VENDOR_KEYS = ("chat_template_kwargs",)

_LOOPBACK_HOSTS = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1", "[::1]")


def _norm_base(url: str) -> str:
    return (url or "").strip().rstrip("/").lower()


def _is_llama_server(base_url: str, local_base_url: str = LOCAL_BASE_URL) -> bool:
    """True only for llama.cpp / llama-server endpoints.

    Used to keep llama.cpp extensions targeted: they must never reach
    OpenRouter, Cerebras or the M365 proxy, which reject or ignore them.
    """
    url = _norm_base(base_url)
    if not url:
        return False
    if url == _norm_base(local_base_url):
        return True
    host = url.split("//", 1)[-1].split("/", 1)[0].split(":", 1)[0]
    return host in _LOOPBACK_HOSTS and "llama" in url


def _split_vendor_keys(
    payload: dict[str, Any], base_url: str, local_base_url: str = LOCAL_BASE_URL
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Strip llama.cpp vendor keys out of a top-level payload.

    Returns (sdk_kwargs, extra_body). Vendor keys are forwarded to the request
    body ONLY when the target is llama-server; for every other backend they are
    dropped. That keeps them out of the SDK signature no matter which backend is
    being called, which is what caused the production outage.
    """
    sdk_kwargs = dict(payload)
    vendor: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key in LLAMA_VENDOR_KEYS:
        if key in sdk_kwargs:
            vendor[key] = sdk_kwargs.pop(key)
    if not _is_llama_server(base_url, local_base_url):
        vendor = {}
    return sdk_kwargs, vendor


def _prepare_local_payload(
    model: str,
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
    tools: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    *,
    budget_tokens: int = COMPACTION_BUDGET_TOKENS,
    extra: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    # NOTE: deliberately no top-level `chat_template_kwargs` here. It is a
    # llama-server extension and this payload is splatted into the OpenAI SDK by
    # _raw_chat(); it is injected into the request body there instead.
    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": _compact_messages(messages, budget_tokens=budget_tokens),
    }

def build_tool_layer_entry(ctx: int, ctx_source: str) -> dict:
    """The chain's FINAL entry: the copilot tool layer on ras-pc (:8789).

    Same 98,304 ctx ceiling as the raw local model -- the tool layer's context is
    bounded by the model behind it -- but it adds real tool calling, and it has
    its own VPS -> Cerebras -> local fallback so it cannot hard-fail.

    `local_last_resort: true` is the marker the BRIEF6 positional floor
    exemption keys on. It is the SAME marker and the SAME predicate the raw local
    entry used; the tool layer qualifies because its api_base is loopback and it
    sits in the last position of the chain. No cloud model can qualify.
    """
    return {
        "model_name": TOOL_LAYER_ALIAS,
        "litellm_params": {
            "model": f"openai/{TOOL_LAYER_MODEL}",
            "api_base": TOOL_LAYER_API_BASE,
            "api_key": TOOL_LAYER_API_KEY,
            "max_retries": 0,
            "timeout": 600,
        },
        "model_info": {
            "mode": "chat",
            "supports_function_calling": True,
            "supports_vision": False,
            "context_window": int(ctx),
            "context_source": ctx_source,
            # ── auditable last-resort markers (BRIEF6 mechanism, reused) ──
            "local_last_resort": True,
            "local_tool_layer": True,
            "local_model_id": TOOL_LAYER_MODEL,
            "local_context_floor_exempt": True,
            "context_floor_exempt_reason":
                f"last-resort tool-layer entry at {int(ctx)} ctx < {MIN_CONTEXT_LENGTH} "
                "floor; bounded by the local model behind it, kept only as the "
                "chain's final entry",
            "chain_role": "FINAL last-resort entry of the auto chain",
            "local_tunnel": "llm-scout-tunnel.service (ras-pc, reverse SSH -R 8789)",
            "local_service": "copilot-tool-layer.service (127.0.0.1:8789)",
            "tool_layer_internal_fallback": "vps -> cerebras -> local(127.0.0.1:8083)",
        },
    }


def ensure_local_last_resort(model_list: list, ctx: int | None = None,
                             ctx_source: str = "") -> tuple:
    """Install/refresh the local entries and drop duplicates and stale names.

    Two loopback entries are kept, because they are two different things:
      * TOOL_LAYER_ALIAS      (:8789) -- the chain's final last resort.
      * LOCAL_LAST_RESORT_ALIAS (:8083) -- the raw model, direct-address only.

    Previously this function collapsed everything onto one llama-server alias.
    It also used to purge `qwen3-8b-local`/`qwen35-9b-local` as duplicates; those
    are now in LEGACY_LOCAL_ALIASES so the honest rename actually removes the
    lying name from config.yaml instead of leaving it as a second name on the
    same server.

    Returns (tool_layer_alias, removed_aliases).
    """
    if ctx is None:
        ctx, ctx_source = probe_local_model_context()
    tl_entry = build_tool_layer_entry(ctx, ctx_source or "local-server-reported")
    local_entry = build_local_last_resort_entry(ctx, ctx_source or "local-server-reported")
    removed = []
    out = []
    seen_tl = False
    seen_local = False
    for e in model_list or []:
        params = (e or {}).get("litellm_params") or {}
        base = str(params.get("api_base") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
        name = (e or {}).get("model_name")
        if name in LEGACY_LOCAL_ALIASES:
            removed.append(name)
            continue
        if base in LOCAL_API_BASES and name not in LAST_RESORT_ALIASES:
            # Any other loopback alias is a duplicate name on a server we already
            # have an honest entry for.
            removed.append(name)
            continue
        if name == TOOL_LAYER_ALIAS:
            if seen_tl:
                continue
            seen_tl = True
            out.append(tl_entry)
            continue
        if name == LOCAL_LAST_RESORT_ALIAS:
            if seen_local:
                continue
            seen_local = True
            out.append(local_entry)
            continue
        out.append(e)
    if not seen_tl:
        out.append(tl_entry)
    if not seen_local:
        out.append(local_entry)
    model_list[:] = out
    return TOOL_LAYER_ALIAS, removed

    out = []

        if name in LEGACY_LOCAL_ALIASES or name == LOCAL_LAST_RESORT_ALIAS:

fixed:
# ── BRIEF8: benchmark provenance is AUTHORITATIVE ───────────────────────────
# The only accepted source for a DeepSWE number is a web search. llm-scout's
# self-test is a 6-band in-house EXECUTION probe on our own 0-100 scale; its
# own code says it is not comparable to DeepSWE/SWE-bench. On 2026-09-27
# record_self_test() wrote that number into deepswe_score, swe_score AND
# agentic_score, and three NVIDIA entries landed on a flat 100.0 that put them
# at the top of the chain, above genuine 88.6/88.4/85.0 results.
#
# A self-test value belongs in self_test_score and nowhere else. It is never
# summed into, blended with, or substituted for a benchmark number: a model with
# only a self-test result is UNSCORED and sorts last.
BENCHMARK_FIELDS = ("deepswe_score", "swe_score", "agentic_score")

# Sources that may legitimately populate a benchmark field.
SEARCH_SCORE_SOURCES = frozenset({"search"})

# Sources that are explicitly NOT a search. Kept for the audit message so a
# rejected entry says why it was rejected instead of silently going UNSCORED.
NON_SEARCH_SCORE_SOURCES = frozenset({
    "self-test",            # in-house execution probe (record_self_test)
    "self-test-unreachable",  # scout could not reach the model
    "curated",              # hand-maintained constant, not a search
})

# A DeepSWE score is a percentage on a 0-100 scale. Anything above that in a
# benchmark field is a RANK KEY (base score + ctx/tool bonuses, which exceed
# 100 by design) that has been stored or displayed as if it were a score.
BENCHMARK_MAX = 100.0


def score_source_of(model: dict | None) -> str:
    """Normalised provenance string. '' means the pre-BRIEF8 shape."""
    src = (model or {}).get("score_source")
    return str(src).strip().lower() if src is not None else ""


def is_search_sourced(model: dict | None) -> bool:
    """True only when a benchmark value is traceable to a search.

    A MISSING `score_source` is the pre-BRIEF8 shape of a search result:
    search_grounded_swe_benchmark() never wrote the key, which is why the 109
    legitimate entries have none. Those are accepted as legacy search
    provenance. Every EXPLICIT non-search source is rejected, so a self-test
    number can never reach a benchmark field no matter how it got there.
    """
    src = score_source_of(model)
    if not src:
        return True
    return src in SEARCH_SCORE_SOURCES


def benchmark_score(model: dict | None) -> float | None:
    """The rankable DeepSWE score, or None for UNSCORED.

    DeepSWE only, and only when search-sourced. There is deliberately no
    fallback to swe_score or agentic_score: a SWE-bench or agentic number is
    recorded in its own field for reference and is never ranked as if it were
    DeepSWE. None means UNSCORED, which sorts after every scored model.
    """
    if not is_search_sourced(model):
        return None
    return _num((model or {}).get("deepswe_score"))


def guard_benchmark_provenance(model: dict) -> list:
    """Strip every benchmark value that is not a search-sourced DeepSWE.

    This is the assertion BRIEF8 Task A.3 asks for, in recoverable form: a
    non-search source (or an out-of-range value, i.e. a rank key) can never
    persist in a benchmark field. Returns the names of the fields it cleared.
    """
    stripped = []
    if not is_search_sourced(model):
        for f in BENCHMARK_FIELDS:
            if model.get(f) is not None:
                model[f] = None
                stripped.append(f)
        return stripped
    for f in BENCHMARK_FIELDS:
        v = _num(model.get(f))
        if v is not None and not (0.0 <= v <= BENCHMARK_MAX):
            # a rank key (base + ctx/tool bonuses) leaked into a score field
            model[f] = None
            stripped.append(f)
    return stripped


def effective_deepswe(model: dict) -> float | None:
    """DeepSWE for RANKING, or None when the model is UNSCORED.

    Was: DeepSWE falling back to SWE-bench. That fallback is gone — BRIEF8
    makes DeepSWE-from-search the only accepted benchmark, so a model whose
    only number is a SWE-bench or agentic score is UNSCORED, not DeepSWE-scored.
    Uses explicit None checks: `x or y` would treat a real 0.0 as missing.
    """
    return benchmark_score(model)

def record_self_test(model_name: str, result: dict) -> dict:
    """Record an in-house self-test WITHOUT letting it become a benchmark score.

    BRIEF8: this function used to write the self-test number into
    `deepswe_score`, `swe_score` AND `agentic_score` with `self_test_score`
    left as None -- destroying the provenance, not merely duplicating it. Three
    NVIDIA entries ended up on a flat 100.0 and took the top of the chain.

    Now the number lives ONLY in `self_test_score`, every benchmark field is
    explicitly cleared, and `score_source` stays "self-test" so
    is_search_sourced() rejects the entry outright. The model is UNSCORED for
    ranking and sorts after every model with a real DeepSWE result. The
    summary says in-house, and the tier is derived from the self-test bands --
    never presented as a percentage of DeepSWE.
    """
    score = adopt_scout_score(result)
    return {
        "search_status": "failed",
        "score_found": False,
        "score_source": "self-test",
        # hard clear: a benchmark field must never hold a self-test number
        "deepswe_score": None,
        "swe_score": None,
        "agentic_score": None,
        "self_test_score": score,
        "self_test_metric": "llm-scout 6-band in-house execution probe "

def _catalog_supports_tools(meta: dict) -> bool | None:
    """Does the provider catalog say this model can call tools?

    True/False when the catalog answers, None when it says nothing (which is the
    case for every provider except OpenRouter) -- and None must never be read as
    "no", or every model from a metadata-free provider would be judged on the
    weak name fragments alone.
    """
    params = meta.get("supported_parameters")
    if params is None:
        return None
    params = [str(p).lower() for p in params]
    return any(p in ("tools", "tool_choice", "functions") for p in params)


def classify_model_class(model: dict, catalog_meta: dict | None = None) -> str:
    """'coding' | 'non-coding'. BRIEF10 Task C.

    Provider-catalog metadata is used FIRST and the model id/alias second,
    because the name is both over- and under-inclusive: `lyria-3-clip-preview`
    needs the catalog's output modality to be recognised as audio, while
    `qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free` contains no junk fragment and is a coding model.
    Metadata signals used:
      * output_modalities containing audio/image/video -> not a coding model
      * supported_voices (a speech/TTS record) -> not a coding model
      * tags/description saying guard/safety AND no tool support -> not coding
    """
    meta = catalog_meta or {}
    outs = [str(x).lower() for x in (meta.get("output_modalities") or [])]
    if any(o in NON_TEXT_OUTPUT for o in outs):
        return "non-coding"
    if meta.get("supported_voices"):
        return "non-coding"
    tools = _catalog_supports_tools(meta)
    # The provider's own words, used only for the classes no coding model has.
    cat_blob = " ".join(str(meta.get(k) or "") for k in
                        ("modality", "description", "tags", "hf_id",
                         "hugging_face_id", "name")).lower()
    # Name/alias: the only place a Cloudflare or NVIDIA id exists.
    namey = " ".join([
        str(model.get("id") or ""), str(model.get("alias") or ""),
        str(model.get("name") or ""),
    ]).lower()
    for frag in NON_CODING_STRONG:
        if frag in namey or frag in cat_blob:
            return "non-coding"
    if tools is False:
        # The catalog knows this model cannot call tools. A bare word like
        # "safety" or "speech" in its description is then decisive; in a coding
        # model that DOES call tools it is not.
        for frag in NON_CODING_WEAK:
            if frag in namey or frag in cat_blob:
                return "non-coding"
    return "coding"

def canonical_benchmark(name) -> str | None:
    """Map whatever the model (or a config) called it to a catalog key.

    Exact alias match first, then a guarded substring pass. The substring pass
    is what stops "SWE-Bench Pro V2 Full" collapsing into "swe-bench-pro":
    the longer key is checked first, so the more specific name wins.
    """
    s = str(name or "").strip().lower()
    if not s:
        return None
    for key, spec in BENCHMARK_CATALOG.items():
        if s == key or s == spec["label"].lower():
            return key
    for key, spec in BENCHMARK_CATALOG.items():
        for a in spec["aliases"]:
            if s == a:
                return key
    for key in sorted(BENCHMARK_CATALOG, key=lambda k: -len(k)):
        spec = BENCHMARK_CATALOG[key]
        if key in s or spec["label"].lower() in s:
            return key
        for a in spec["aliases"]:
            if len(a) >= 6 and a in s:
                return key
    return None


def benchmark_field(key: str) -> str | None:
    spec = BENCHMARK_CATALOG.get(key or "")
    return spec["field"] if spec else None


def benchmark_ceiling(key: str) -> float | None:
    spec = BENCHMARK_CATALOG.get(key or "")
    return float(spec["ceiling"]) if spec else None


def benchmark_label(key: str) -> str:
    spec = BENCHMARK_CATALOG.get(key or "")
    return spec["label"] if spec else str(key or "")


def plausible_benchmark_score(key: str, score) -> bool:
    """Range + plausibility gate for a benchmark value, before any provenance.

    Rejects: unknown benchmark, non-numeric, outside 0..ceiling (which is what
    catches a rank key stored as a score), and exact zero.
    """
    val = _num(score)
    if val is None:
        return False
    ceiling = benchmark_ceiling(key)
    if ceiling is None:
        return False
    if not (0.0 <= val <= ceiling):
        return False
    if val < BENCHMARK_MIN_PLAUSIBLE:
        return False
    return True


# ── live-source verification: the guarantee BRIEF10 did not have ────────────


def _html_to_text(raw: str) -> str:
    """Tags out, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed.

    Deliberately crude. It only has to make a published number findable in
    leaderboard HTML, and being crude is safe: it can merge neighbouring text
    (which loses nothing, since we then require the number and the model name
    to co-occur) but it cannot invent a number that was not in the bytes.
    """
    import html as _html
    t = re.sub(r"(?is)<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>", " ", str(raw or ""))
    t = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", t)
    t = _html.unescape(t)
    t = t.replace(",", "")
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t)


def _numeric_tokens(text: str) -> list:
    out = []
    for tok in re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", str(text or "")):
        n = _num(tok)
        if n is not None:
            out.append(n)
    return out


def resolve_source_url(url: str, opener=None) -> tuple:
    """Follow a grounding redirect to the real publisher page.

    Task A showed Gemini returns
    `vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/...` blobs. They do
    resolve, but a redirect URL is not auditable provenance -- it expires and
    hides the publisher. So the canonical URL is what gets STORED. A 404 is
    surfaced rather than swallowed: one of Task A's three URLs was dead.
    """
    raw = str(url or "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return None, 0, "no_url"
    if not raw.lower().startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        return None, 0, "not_a_url"
    op = opener or urllib.request
    req = urllib.request.Request(raw, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; litellm-refresh/1.0)"})
    try:
        with op.urlopen(req, timeout=LIVE_FETCH_TIMEOUT) as resp:
            return resp.geturl(), int(getattr(resp, "status", 200) or 200), None
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return raw, int(e.code), f"http_{e.code}"
    except Exception as e:
        return raw, 0, f"{type(e).__name__}"


def fetch_page_text(url: str, opener=None) -> tuple:
    """(text, status, error). Never raises."""
    op = opener or urllib.request
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; litellm-refresh/1.0)"})
    try:
        with op.urlopen(req, timeout=LIVE_FETCH_TIMEOUT) as resp:
            raw = resp.read()
            return _html_to_text(raw.decode("utf-8", "ignore")), int(getattr(resp, "status", 200) or 200), None
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return "", int(e.code), f"http_{e.code}"
    except Exception as e:
        return "", 0, f"{type(e).__name__}"


def verify_live_source(url: str, score, model_tokens=(), opener=None,
                       max_excerpt: int = 400) -> tuple:
    """(ok, reason, canonical_url, excerpt). The number must be ON THE PAGE.

    `model_tokens` are the caller's normalised spellings of the model (e.g.
    {"gpt-oss-120b", "gpt-oss-120-high"}). They are required to co-occur on
    the page, but deliberately NOT required to be adjacent to the number:
    leaderboards put the name in one column and the score in another, and
    demanding adjacency is what produced Task A's column misattribution.

    This function is the only thing that decides. A model can assert anything;
    it cannot put a number on a page that does not have it.
    """
    val = _num(score)
    if val is None:
        return False, "no_number_returned", None, None
    canonical, status, err = resolve_source_url(url, opener=opener)
    if err or status >= 400 or not canonical:
        return False, (err or f"http_{status}"), None, None
    text, status2, err2 = fetch_page_text(canonical, opener=opener)
    if err2 or status2 >= 400 or not text.strip():
        return False, (err2 or f"http_{status2}"), canonical, None
    if not score_appears_in_snippet(val, text):
        return False, "number_not_on_live_page", canonical, None
    toks = {str(t).strip().lower() for t in (model_tokens or ()) if str(t).strip()}
    if toks and not any(t in text.lower() for t in toks):
        return False, "model_name_not_on_live_page", canonical, None
    # Excerpt: the number with a little context, so a human auditing the cache
    # sees the actual row rather than having to re-fetch the page.
    excerpt = None
    for m in re.finditer(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", text):
        n = _num(m.group(0))
        if n is not None and abs(n - val) <= 1e-9:
            excerpt = text[max(0, m.start() - max_excerpt // 2): m.end() + max_excerpt // 2].strip()
            break
    return True, "verified_on_live_page", canonical, excerpt


# ── direct leaderboard parsing: the source that needs no model at all ───────


def _norm_model_token(s: str) -> str:
    """Lowercase, strip vendor prefixes, punctuation and size suffixes."""
    s = str(s or "").strip().lower()
    s = re.sub(r"^(?:openrouter|hf|models|api|cloudflare-ai|nvidia|deepinfra|"
               r"together-ai|fireworks-ai|novita|nebius|x-ai)[/:]+", "", s)
    s = s.split("/")[-1]
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s)
    return s.strip("-")


def model_name_variants(model_id: str, model_name: str = "") -> list:
    """Plausible published spellings of a catalog model id.

    Aider prints "gpt-oss-120b (high)", Scale prints "gpt-oss-120b", OpenRouter
    prints "openai/gpt-oss-120b". All of them must resolve to the same model,
    so all of them are accepted spellings -- and the live page must still
    contain one of them, or the number is rejected.
    """
    out = []
    for raw in (model_id, model_name):
        v = _norm_model_token(raw)
        if v and v not in out:
            out.append(v)
    mid = _norm_model_token(model_id)
    if mid.endswith("-it"):
        b = mid[:-3]
        if b and b not in out:
            out.append(b)
    if mid.endswith("-instruct"):
        b = mid[:-9]
        if b and b not in out:
            out.append(b)
    return out


def parse_scale_swe_pro(text: str, variants) -> tuple:
    """Pull (score, excerpt) for one model out of the Scale SWE-bench Pro board.

    The page embeds its leaderboard as JSON, which is far more reliable than
    scraping the table: `{"model":"gpt-oss-120b","score":16.2,"rank":19}`. The
    `model` key is matched EXACTLY against a variant, so a number can never be
    picked up from a neighbouring row the way a proximity scan would.
    """
    if not variants:
        return None, None
    for m in re.finditer(r'"model"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', text):
        name = _norm_model_token(m.group(1))
        if name not in variants:
            continue
        window = text[m.start(): m.start() + 400]
        sm = re.search(r'"score"\s*:\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)', window)
        if not sm:
            continue
        val = _num(sm.group(1))
        if val is None:
            continue
        return val, text[max(0, m.start() - 120): m.start() + 320].strip()
    return None, None


def parse_aider_polyglot(text: str, variants) -> tuple:
    """Pull (score, excerpt) out of the Aider polyglot leaderboard.

    The FIRST percentage after the model name is the one to take. Task A
    measured what happens if you are not careful here: one row reads
    `gpt-oss-120b (high) 41.8% $0.74 ... 79.1% diff` -- 79.1 is a real number
    for the same model but it is the `diff` EDIT-FORMAT variant, a different
    metric on a different column. Taking the first `%` yields 41.8, which is
    the polyglot score; taking the second is exactly the misattribution the
    live-fetch step alone would NOT have caught, since 79.1 is also on the page.
    Cost and wall-clock appear in the row too (`$0.74`, `12.2 s/case`) and are
    skipped because they are not percentages.
    """
    if not variants:
        return None, None
    low = text.lower()
    for v in variants:
        for m in re.finditer(re.escape(v), low):
            tail = text[m.end(): m.end() + 200]
            pm = re.search(r"(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*%", tail)
            if not pm:
                continue
            val = _num(pm.group(1))
            if val is None:
                continue
            if not plausible_benchmark_score("aider-polyglot", val):
                continue
            return val, text[max(0, m.start() - 80): m.end() + 200].strip()
    return None, None


_DIRECT_PARSERS = {
    "aider": parse_aider_polyglot,
    "scale_swe_pro": parse_scale_swe_pro,
}


def fetch_direct_benchmark_score(model_id: str, model_name: str,
                                 opener=None) -> dict | None:
    """Read a published number straight out of a public leaderboard.

    This is the strongest unofficial evidence available, and it needs no model
    at all: the number is parsed from the publisher's own page, so "is the
    number really there" is true by construction rather than by trust. It also
    sidesteps the Gemini grounding quota entirely.

    Returns a provenance dict, or None when no direct source carries a
    plausible number for this model. "None" is a real answer: it means this
    particular model is not on these particular boards.
    """
    variants = model_name_variants(model_id, model_name)
    for key, spec in DIRECT_BENCHMARK_SOURCES.items():
        url = spec["url"]
        text, status, err = fetch_page_text(url, opener=opener)
        if err or status >= 400 or not text.strip():
            continue
        parser = _DIRECT_PARSERS.get(spec["parser"])
        if parser is None:
            continue
        try:
            val, excerpt = parser(text, variants)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if val is None or not plausible_benchmark_score(key, val):
            continue
        if not score_appears_in_snippet(val, text):
            continue
        if not any(v in text.lower() for v in variants):
            continue
        return {
            "benchmark": key,
            "benchmark_label": benchmark_label(key),
            "score": round(float(val), 1),
            "source": "tier2-direct",
            "url": url,
            "canonical_url": url,
            "snippet": (excerpt or "")[:600],
            "verified": True,
            "verification": "parsed_from_live_page",
            "model_variants": variants,
            "at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
        }
    return None


def record_benchmark_score(model: dict, prov: dict) -> list:
    """Write a verified unofficial number into ITS OWN field, with provenance.

    Returns the list of fields written. Refuses anything that is not a
    catalogued benchmark with a verified number -- so there is no code path that
    can put a SWE-bench number into `deepswe_score`.
    """
    key = prov.get("benchmark")
    field = benchmark_field(key)
    if field is None or not prov.get("verified"):
        return []
    score = _num(prov.get("score"))
    if score is None or not plausible_benchmark_score(key, score):
        return []
    if not prov.get("url"):
        return []
    model[field] = round(float(score), 1)
    model["score_benchmark"] = key
    model["score_benchmark_label"] = benchmark_label(key)
    model["score_found"] = True
    model["search_status"] = "ok"
    model["evaluated_at"] = prov.get("at") or datetime.now().isoformat()
    # Per-benchmark provenance, keyed by benchmark so two benchmarks can never
    # overwrite each other's evidence.
    per = model.get("bench_provenance")
    if not isinstance(per, dict):
        per = {}
    per[key] = {
        "score": round(float(score), 1),
        "label": benchmark_label(key),
        "source": prov.get("source"),
        "url": prov.get("url"),
        "canonical_url": prov.get("canonical_url") or prov.get("url"),
        "snippet": (prov.get("snippet") or "")[:600],
        "verification": prov.get("verification"),
        "verified": True,
        "at": prov.get("at") or datetime.now().isoformat(),
    }
    model["bench_provenance"] = per
    return [field, "score_benchmark", "bench_provenance"]


# The per-benchmark score fields join BENCHMARK_FIELDS so that every existing
# guard -- guard_benchmark_provenance(), retire_untiered_score() and the audit
# -- automatically covers them. That is the point: a benchmark number with no
# trustworthy tier is retired by the same code that already retires a fabricated
# DeepSWE number, instead of being a new hole beside a repaired one.
for _k, _spec in BENCHMARK_CATALOG.items():
    if _spec["field"] not in BENCHMARK_FIELDS:
        BENCHMARK_FIELDS = BENCHMARK_FIELDS + (_spec["field"],)
del _k, _spec


def benchmark_fields_of(model: dict | None) -> dict:
    """{benchmark_key: score} for every catalogued benchmark this model has."""
    out = {}
    for key, spec in BENCHMARK_CATALOG.items():
        v = _num((model or {}).get(spec["field"]))
        if v is not None and plausible_benchmark_score(key, v):
            out[key] = v
    return out


def effective_benchmark(model: dict | None) -> tuple:
    """The one number used for ordering, as (benchmark_key, value).

    DeepSWE wins when present, because it is the benchmark the whole catalog
    was built around and the only one with an official board. Otherwise the
    model has exactly one unofficial benchmark recorded (the common case), and
    that is returned with its benchmark name attached so no caller can ever
    compare it to a DeepSWE number without saying which it is.
    """
    fields = benchmark_fields_of(model)
    if not fields:
        return None, None
    if DEEPSWE_BENCHMARK in fields:
        return DEEPSWE_BENCHMARK, fields[DEEPSWE_BENCHMARK]
    if len(fields) == 1:
        return next(iter(fields))
    # More than one non-DeepSWE benchmark: no principled way to pick, so
    # UNSCORED for ordering rather than an arbitrary maximum.
    return None, None


# ── Task E: ordering with an honest signal ─────────────────────────────────
#
# Rule implemented: a TIER 2 model never outranks a TIER 1 model whose
# OFFICIAL score is higher.

def tier2_direct_lookup(model_id: str, model_name: str, provider: str,
                        frontier: float | None, opener=None) -> dict | None:
    """BRIEF11 Task B: read a number straight off a public leaderboard.

    Tried BEFORE the Gemini search. It is stronger evidence (the number is
    parsed from the publisher's page rather than quoted at second hand), it
    costs no grounding quota, and it cannot be faked by a model. If a board
    carries this model, this is all the Tier 2 machinery that is needed.

    prov = fetch_direct_benchmark_score(model_id, model_name, opener=opener)

        if _num(prov["score"]) > frontier + TIER2_MARGIN:
            return None
    log(f"  -> [{provider}] {model_id}: UNOFFICIAL {prov['score']} "
        f"({prov['benchmark_label']}) read directly from {prov['url']}")

        base["score_provenance"] = direct

def normalise_opinion_bucket(value) -> str | None:
    s = str(value or "").strip().lower().replace("_", "-").replace(" ", "-")

        return s
    if s in ("unknown", "unsure", "no-information", "noinfo", "n-a", "na"):
        return "unknown"

def _gemini_json(prompt: str, timeout: int = 35) -> tuple:
    """One grounded Gemini call -> (parsed dict | None, error str | None)."""
    url = ("https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/"
           f"gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent?key={GEMINI_API_KEY}")
    payload = {"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": prompt}]}],
               "tools": [{"google_search": {}}],
               "generationConfig": {"temperature": 0.0}}
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            res = json.load(resp)
    except Exception as e:
        return None, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
    parts = (res.get("candidates") or [{}])[0].get("content", {}).get("parts", [{}])
    text = "".join(p.get("text", "") for p in parts)
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.DOTALL)
    if not m:
        return None, "no_json_in_response"
    try:
        out = json.loads(m.group(0))
    except Exception:
        return None, "unparseable_json"
    return (out, None) if isinstance(out, dict) else (None, "not_an_object")

    base = {

        "opinion": None, "score_source": "tier3-opinion",
        "evaluated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),

    prompt = TIER3_PROMPT.format(model_id=model_id, model_name=model_name,
                                 provider=provider)
    seen, errors = [], []
    for _ in range(max(1, int(runs))):
        parsed, err = _gemini_json(prompt)
        if err:
            errors.append(err)

        base["error"] = errors[0] if errors else "no_response"
        base["evaluated_at"] = None

    good = [b for b in buckets if b and b != "unknown"]
    if len(good) < len(seen):
        base["opinion_declined"] = True
        base["opinion_buckets"] = buckets
        base["search_status"] = "ok"

        # is noise. Recorded as such so the audit can show it was considered.

        base["opinion_buckets"] = buckets
        base["search_status"] = "ok"

            f"({buckets})")
        return base
    bucket = good[0]

        "opinion": {
            "bucket": bucket,
            "bucket_rank": OPINION_BUCKET_RANK[bucket],
            "reasoning": str(seen[0].get("reasoning") or "")[:600],
            "sources": [s for s in (seen[0].get("sources") or []) if s][:6],
            "kind": "comparative-opinion",
            "is_measurement": False,
            "runs_agreed": len(good),
            "at": datetime.now().isoformat(),

        "opinion_buckets": buckets,

        f"(reproduced {len(good)}x) - not a measurement")

T_TIER1, T_TIER2, T_TIER3, T_NONE = 0, 1, 2, 3


def annotate_tier2_ranks(models) -> None:
    """Give every Tier 2 model a WITHIN-BENCHMARK percentile, in place.

    Why percentiles and not the raw number: 16.2 on SWE-bench Pro and 41.8 on
    Aider polyglot are not rival readings of one scale, and ordering them
    against each other by their printed values would be a category error. The
    DeepSWE literature documents these benchmarks disagreeing substantially on
    the same model, which is the whole reason BRIEF11 forbids letting a
    SWE-bench number be compared as a DeepSWE one.

    A percentile is the one defensible cross-benchmark statement: "this model is
    in the top quarter of the models we have a real number for ON THIS
    BENCHMARK". Models whose benchmark has a single observation get no
    percentile and are marked as unranked-within-benchmark -- they are still
    Tier 2, they just cannot be said to lead anything.

    Mutates in place (main() calls this once, before sorting).
    """
    by_bench: dict = {}
    for m in models:
        bench, val = effective_benchmark(m)
        if bench is None or val is None:
            continue
        tier = str(m.get("score_tier") or "").strip().lower()
        if tier != "unofficial":

        by_bench.setdefault(bench, []).append((m, val))
    for bench, rows in by_bench.items():
        vals = sorted({v for _m, v in rows})
        for m, val in rows:
            m["tier2_benchmark"] = bench
            m["tier2_benchmark_label"] = benchmark_label(bench)
            if len(vals) < 2:
                m["tier2_percentile"] = None
                m["tier2_rank_note"] = ("only model we have a real number for on "
                                        f"{benchmark_label(bench)}; nothing to "
                                        "compare it against")
            else:
                # fraction of same-benchmark values this one beats
                below = sum(1 for v in vals if v < val)
                equal = sum(1 for v in vals if v == val)
                m["tier2_percentile"] = round(
                    100.0 * (below + 0.5 * (equal - 1)) / (len(vals) - 1), 1)
                m["tier2_rank_note"] = (
                    f"{benchmark_label(bench)} percentile among "
                    f"{len(vals)} model(s) with a verified number")

    """Which tier this model is in. The one definition of "how good is this
    evidence", used by the sort, the audit and the chain listing alike."""
    tier = str(model.get("score_tier") or "").strip().lower()
    bench, val = effective_benchmark(model)
    if tier == "official" and bench == DEEPSWE_BENCHMARK and val is not None:
        return T_TIER1
    if tier == "unofficial" and val is not None:
        return T_TIER2
    if opinion_bucket(model)[0]:
        return T_TIER3
    return T_NONE


def tiered_sort_key(model: dict):
    """Ascending key for `list.sort()`: the LOWEST key must be the BEST model.

    Bands, then evidence strength inside the band, then the value NEGATED. The
    negation is the part that is easy to get backwards -- main() calls
    `ranked_models.sort(key=tiered_sort_key)`, so a plain score here would put
    the worst model at the top of the config.
    """
    band = score_band(model)
    frs = _num(model.get("final_rank_score"))
    if band == T_TIER1:
        return (T_TIER1, frs is None, -(frs if frs is not None else 0.0))
    if band == T_TIER2:
        # final_rank_score is the DeepSWE rank key, which is None for a model
        # whose only number is on another benchmark. Within Tier 2 the
        # within-benchmark percentile decides, and the benchmark name is only a
        # stable tie-break: two different benchmarks are never ordered against
        # each other by their printed numbers.
        pct = _num(model.get("tier2_percentile"))
        bench = str(model.get("tier2_benchmark") or "")
        return (T_TIER2, pct is None, -(pct if pct is not None else 0.0), bench)
    if band == T_TIER3:
        _bucket, rank = opinion_bucket(model)
        return (T_TIER3, rank is None, -(rank if rank is not None else 0.0))
    # No trusted number and no opinion. A leftover `final_rank_score` from a
    # retired untiered value must NOT order these models: the whole point of the
    # repair is that a fabricated 88.6 is indistinguishable from no score. They
    # stay equal and keep discovery order (sort is stable).
    return (T_NONE, 1, 0.0)


def describe_score(model: dict) -> str:
    """One line a reader can audit, that never mixes a measurement with a guess."""
    band = score_band(model)
    if band == T_TIER1:
        return f"TIER1 official DeepSWE {model.get('deepswe_score')}"
    if band == T_TIER2:
        return (f"TIER2 cited {model.get('score_benchmark_label') or model.get('tier2_benchmark')} "
                f"{model.get(model.get('tier2_benchmark') and BENCHMARK_CATALOG.get(model['tier2_benchmark'], {}).get('field') or '', None)}"
                f" ({model.get('score_evidence') or 'cited'})")
    if band == T_TIER3:
        bucket, _r = opinion_bucket(model)
        return f"TIER3 opinion only: {bucket} (NOT a measurement)"
    return "unscored"

class _CallableOpener:
    """Adapts a plain `urlopen`-shaped callable to the module-like interface.

    Without this, passing a function instead of a module fails with
    `AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'urlopen'` -- which is
    swallowed into a reason string and then looks exactly like a network
    failure. That is a genuinely expensive bug to chase, so both spellings are
    accepted and the mistake surfaces as a clear TypeError at the boundary.
    """

    def __init__(self, fn):
        self.urlopen = fn


def _as_opener(opener):
    if opener is None:
        return urllib.request
    if hasattr(opener, "urlopen"):
        return opener
    if callable(opener):
        return _CallableOpener(opener)
    raise TypeError(
        f"opener must be a module-like object with .urlopen, or a callable "
        f"taking (request, timeout); got {type(opener).__name__}")


def resolve_source_url(url: str, opener=None) -> tuple:
    """Follow a grounding redirect to the real publisher page.

    Task A showed Gemini returns
    `vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/...` blobs. They do
    resolve, but a redirect URL is not auditable provenance -- it expires and
    hides the publisher. So the canonical URL is what gets STORED. A 404 is
    surfaced rather than swallowed: one of Task A's three URLs was dead.

    if not raw:
        return None, 0, "no_url"
    if not raw.lower().startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        return None, 0, "not_a_url"
    op = _as_opener(opener)
    req = urllib.request.Request(raw, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; litellm-refresh/1.0)"})
    try:
        with op.urlopen(req, timeout=LIVE_FETCH_TIMEOUT) as resp:

        # only diagnostic a caller gets.
        return raw, 0, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"


def fetch_page_text(url: str, opener=None) -> tuple:
    """(text, status, error). Never raises."""
    op = _as_opener(opener)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; litellm-refresh/1.0)"})
    try:
        with op.urlopen(req, timeout=LIVE_FETCH_TIMEOUT) as resp:
            raw = resp.read()
            return _html_to_text(raw.decode("utf-8", "ignore")), int(getattr(resp, "status", 200) or 200), None
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return "", int(e.code), f"http_{e.code}"
    except Exception as e:
        return "", 0, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"

def search_browser(query: str, *, timeout_ms: int = SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS) -> dict:
    """Search the web in a BROKER-LEASED CloakBrowser window.

    Isolation contract:
      * acquire_window() gets this process its own window (the broker assigns
        real CDP targetIds), so the Copilot browser and other harnesses are
        untouched.
      * every tab is closed and the lease released in `finally`, including on
        timeout or exception, so nothing leaks.
    """
    from cloakbrowser_agent import acquire_window

    win = None
    tabs: list = []
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        win = acquire_window(LEASE_CLIENT)
        page = win.new_tab("about:blank")
        tabs.append(page)
        # duckduckgo lite: server-rendered, no consent wall, easy to parse
        url = "https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=" + urllib.request.quote(query)
        page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=timeout_ms)
        time.sleep(1.2)
        text = page.inner_text("body")
        try:
            links = page.eval_on_selector_all(
                "a.result-link, a[href^='http']",
                "els => els.slice(0,25).map(e => e.textContent.trim())",
            )
        except Exception:
            links = []
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "query": query,
            "window": repr(win),
            "results": [_strip(x) for x in (links or []) if _strip(x)][:20],
            "text": _strip(text)[:4000],
            "elapsed_s": round(time.time() - t0, 2),
        }
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"ok": False, "query": query, "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300],
                "elapsed_s": round(time.time() - t0, 2)}
    finally:
        # CLOSE OUR BROWSER WORK -- tabs first, then the lease.
        for t in tabs:
            try:
                win.close_tab(t)
            except Exception:
                pass
        if win is not None:
            try:
                win.close()
            except Exception:

# ATS error pages that discovery hands us as if they were job postings.
# Kept to strings only ever emitted by a 404/withdrawn-posting template —
# never generic words like "expired" that a real job title could contain.
_DEAD_POSTING_MARKERS = (
    'this page seems to have vanished',
    'page seems to have vanished',
    'page not found',
    'page you are looking for',
    'page cannot be found',
    "can't find the page",
    'cannot find the page',
    'this job is no longer available',
    'job is no longer available',
    'no longer exists',
    'job posting has expired',
    'this job has been closed',
    'position has been filled',
    'no longer accepting applications',
    'job has been filled',
    'posting has been removed',
)


def _dead_posting_title(title: str) -> bool:
    """True when a discovered job's own title is an ATS error template.

    Discovery keeps returning 404 pages (a Greenhouse "MyGreenhouse" URL whose
    real title is "This page seems to have vanished"). Applying to one burns
    the entire job deadline — measured 605999ms against a dead page while the
    resume pipeline waited on a rate-limited Gemini — so it must be rejected
    before any resume generation or form navigation starts.
    """
    t = (title or '').strip().lower()
    if not t:
        return False
    return any(marker in t for marker in _DEAD_POSTING_MARKERS)


async def apply_to_job(page, job: dict, resume: dict, resume_pdf_path: str, dry_run: bool, blank_run: bool, smoke_run: bool = False) -> dict:
    main_page = page
    _adopted_popup = None
    result = {
        'status': 'unknown',
        'job_description': '',
        'resume_pdf_path': resume_pdf_path,
    }

    try:
        print(f'\n[APPLY] {job["title"]} @ {job["company"]}')

        # Reject dead postings before anything expensive happens: no goto, no
        # tailored-resume build, no form fill — those all cost minutes and the
        # deadline belongs to a job that exists.
        if _dead_posting_title(job.get('title', '')):
            print(f'  [APPLY] Dead posting detected from title '
                  f'({job["title"][:60]!r}) — skipping, no deadline spent.')
            result['status'] = 'dead_posting'
            result['notes'] = f'ATS error page, not a posting: {job.get("title", "")}'
            return result

    # the best verified reading rather than whichever sentence parsed first.

    best: dict = {}

    for prov in accepted:

        if k is None:

        if k == DEEPSWE_BENCHMARK:
            official_only.append(prov)
            continue
        cur = best.get(k)
        if cur is None or (prov.get("score") or 0) > (cur.get("score") or 0):
            best[k] = prov
    out = {
        "search_status": "ok", "score_found": bool(best),
        "score_source": "browser-ai-mode", **blank_benchmark_fields(),
        "coding_tier": None, "supports_tool_calls": None,

def numbers_in(text: str) -> list:
    """Every SCORE in `text`, in order, as floats. Percent signs are stripped by
    the regex itself, so '62.4%' reads as 62.4.

    Digits that belong to a metric name are excluded first, so `pass@1 = 63.4`
    yields [63.4] and never [1.0, 63.4]. A 1.0 harvested out of `pass@1` is
    not a cosmetic wart: it is plausible enough to clear the per-benchmark
    sanity ceiling, and it would then be preferred over the real reading.
    """

def benchmark_mentions(text: str) -> list:
    """(benchmark_key, start, end) for every benchmark NAMED in `text`.

    Longer keys are matched first and a span already claimed by a longer name is
    not re-claimed, so "swe-bench-pro" does not also register as a bare
    "swe-bench" mention.
    """
    s = str(text or "").lower()
    found, taken = [], []
    for key in sorted(BENCHMARK_CATALOG, key=lambda k: -len(k)):
        spec = BENCHMARK_CATALOG[key]
        names = [key, spec["label"].lower()] + list(spec["aliases"])
        for a in names:
            a = str(a or "").lower()
            if len(a) < 4:
                continue
            start = 0
            while True:
                i = s.find(a, start)
                if i < 0:
                    break
                span = (i, i + len(a))
                if not any(span[0] >= t[0] and span[1] <= t[1] for t in taken):
                    taken.append(span)
                    found.append((key, span[0], span[1]))
                start = i + 1
    return found


def benchmark_for_number(sentence: str, number, n_start=None, n_end=None):
    """The benchmark THIS number was reported on, or None.

    BRIEF13 B.3/B.4, and the bug this exists to prevent: asking
    `canonical_benchmark()` about a whole sentence returns the FIRST benchmark
    the sentence names, so

        "gpt-oss-120b reaches 62.4% on SWE-bench Verified and 16.2% on
         SWE-bench Pro."

    files BOTH numbers under SWE-bench Verified. That is precisely the conflation
    the brief names -- 62.4 and 16.2 are different benchmarks and the whole
    reason the two have their own fields.

    So each number is bound to its NEAREST benchmark mention. A mention that
    FOLLOWS the number ("62.4% on SWE-bench Verified") is the English
    convention and wins a tie, because "Benchmark: 63.4" and "63.4 on
    Benchmark" are both common and the trailing one is the more frequent shape in
    leaderboard prose and AI Mode answers.
    """
    if n_start is None:
        n_start, n_end = 0, 0
    mentions = benchmark_mentions(sentence)
    if not mentions:
        return None
    best = None
    for key, ms, me in mentions:
        if n_end <= ms:
            gap, after = ms - n_end, True
        elif me <= n_start:
            gap, after = n_start - me, False
        else:
            gap, after = 0, True      # the number is inside the mention itself
        cand = (gap, 0 if after else 1, key)
        if best is None or cand < best[0]:
            best = (cand, key)
    return best[1] if best else None

      1. the text must NOT look like a pre-submit checklist, and
      2. the text MUST contain an actual positive confirmation phrase.

    Guard 2 was missing. The old version returned True for any dict with
    non-empty text, so `applications_log.json` ended up with entries whose
    "confirmation" was a CSS blob ("...opacity overlay behaviour is not
    applied) */ --cnvs-sys-depth-6: 0 0.375rem ...") and 17 entries carrying
    the bare marker "applied" — a word that was dropped from the applier's
    SUCCESS_KEYWORDS on 2026-09-05 precisely because it matched too much.
    """
    if not isinstance(confirmation, dict):
        return False
    marker = str(confirmation.get('marker') or '')
    context = str(confirmation.get('context') or '')
    if not marker and not context:
        return False
    combined = '%s %s' % (marker, context)
    if any(rx.search(combined) for rx in _NOT_SUBMITTED_RES):
        return False
    # Require positive proof. The marker is checked on its own because it is
    # written from SUCCESS_KEYWORDS; the context only counts as a fallback
    # for older entries whose marker is missing.
    keywords = _applier_success_keywords()
    if marker and keywords:
        if any(k.strip().lower() in marker.strip().lower() for k in keywords):
            return True
    elif marker and not keywords and _POSITIVE_PROOF_RE.search(marker):
        return True
    if context and _POSITIVE_PROOF_RE.search(context):
        return True
    return False

def to_ogg_opus(src: Path, dst: Path) -> Path:
    """Convert to the mono 48 kHz OGG/Opus that Telegram requires for voice notes.

    ``-f opus`` is explicit because callers pass their own destination name (the
    call agent asks for a ``.wav`` path); otherwise ffmpeg picks the muxer from
    the extension and refuses to put an Opus stream in a file named ``.wav``.
    """
    _run(
        [
            FFMPEG, "-nostdin", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y",
            "-i", str(src), "-map", "0:a:0", "-vn",
            "-ac", "1", "-ar", "48000", "-c:a", "libopus", "-b:a", "32k",
            "-application", "audio", "-vbr", "on", "-f", "opus", str(dst),
        ],
        "ffmpeg opus conversion failed",
        capture_output=True,
        timeout=AUDIO_TIMEOUT,
    )
    return Path(dst)
